items.evidence: No ball and free hit. A no ball is called most often when the bowler's front foot lands fully beyond the popping crease, or for a full toss above waist height. It adds one run to the batting side and is not a legal ball. In T20 cricket the next delivery after a front-foot no ball is a free hit: the batter can only be out in ways such as run out, not bowled, caught or lbw.
items.claim: After a front-foot no ball, the next delivery is a free hit.
items.label: supported

items.evidence: Leg before wicket (LBW). A batter is out lbw when the ball would have gone on to hit the stumps but hit the batter's body first, subject to conditions. The ball must not pitch outside leg stump. If the batter plays a shot, the impact must be in line with the stumps. If the batter offers no shot, impact outside off stump can still be out.
items.claim: A batter cannot be out lbw if the ball pitches outside leg stump.
items.label: supported

items.evidence: [doc:rule-decision-review-system-drs] Decision Review System (DRS). DRS lets a team challenge an on-field umpire's decision using ball tracking, edge detection (UltraEdge or Snicko) and replays. In the IPL each team gets a limited number of unsuccessful reviews per innings. For lbw, an "umpire's call" result means the on-field decision stands because the ball tracking was marginal, and the team keeps its review. Note: DRS was introduced to the IPL in 2018, after the seasons covered by this dataset.
items.claim: In the IPL each team gets a limited number of unsuccessful reviews per innings.
items.label: supported
